description.p: Polyglot AI is a desktop coding assistant for Linux that supports multiple AI providers including OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and DeepSeek. It provides a full IDE-like interface with a code editor, file explorer, AI chat panel, code review tools, and integrated terminal.
On Windows, a cancelled database backup that had to be given up on no longer leaves its half-written file on disk.

Cancel now stops a database backup while the database is busy with one query, for example one that is waiting for a lock. Before, a built-in export could only be cancelled between batches of rows. Nothing is left on disk after a cancelled backup.

Cancel now stops a database restore while a statement is running, for example one that is waiting for a lock. Before, a restore of a built-in export could only be cancelled between statements. The message says what was changed: nothing on PostgreSQL, and how many statements were applied on MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server and Oracle.

A saved database connection can be deleted: select it and click the bin next to the pencil. You are asked first, the database itself is not touched, and its query history and snippets are kept unless you choose to delete them too. On Windows, saving settings and connections a second time no longer fails.

The Database panel can back up a database to a file and restore it: with the engine's own tools for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite, or with a built-in SQL export that also covers SQL Server and Oracle. A restore says what it will do before it changes anything, and Cancel stops it. After connecting, the panel lists the server's databases and the tables in each. Saved connections can be edited, and the SQL editor highlights what you type. In the AWS panel, right-click an RDS database to list its snapshots or create one. SQL Server errors now read as a plain sentence.

The Database panel now connects to SQL Server and Oracle as well as PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite, which covers every Amazon RDS engine except Db2. Connections can require encryption and check the server's certificate, go through an SSH bastion or AWS Session Manager to reach a database in a private network, and sign in with an AWS IAM token instead of a password. In the AWS panel, right-click an RDS database and choose "Connect in Database panel" to open the connection dialog already filled in. Passwords containing @, /, : or # now work. The .deb also asks for the system libraries Qt needs, so it starts on a minimal Debian or Ubuntu install.

The Fedora and RHEL package starts again: in 0.18.16 to 0.18.19 its launcher pointed at a folder that no longer existed after installation, so the polyglot-ai command failed with "No such file or directory". Both the .deb and the .rpm now really install with no network connection, using the exact dependency versions each release is tested with, on Python 3.11 to 3.14 (and 3.15 for the .rpm). Before this release the bundled packages only matched the Python of the build machine, and every other system quietly downloaded newer, untested versions instead.

The AI's AWS tools now use the profile and region selected in the AWS panel, and the approval card shows them. Read-only AWS commands (describe, list, get) run without a prompt; anything that changes state, returns stored data or credentials, or touches a local file still asks. Before this release every AWS command asked, and bootstrap mode never skipped a prompt; both now work as described. In the AWS panel, S3 buckets show their region and a summary of public access, encryption and versioning; EKS, DynamoDB, SQS and SNS rows show a status and a count; access-denied messages name the action that was refused; ECS lists faster; and the list of empty services wraps instead of being cut off.

AWS panel fixes. The details pane no longer keeps showing a resource that has gone from the list, and switching profile or region clears the old rows and details straight away. Typing a region no longer refreshes on every keystroke. Stop, Start, Reboot and Force new deployment refresh the list when they finish, and a listing that was cut short says so. SSO and service settings in the AWS config no longer appear as profiles. The AI now asks before reading table data or credentials from AWS, before using a local file as an argument, and before any call that writes a file.

The AWS panel now covers EC2, Lambda, ECS, EKS, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, CloudFormation stacks and CloudWatch alarms. Clicking a resource shows a readable summary above the full output, every resource opens in the AWS Console with one click, sections show visible expand/collapse arrows, and a filter narrows the list. ECS lists every service in a cluster, and EKS clusters can be added to your kubeconfig for the Kubernetes panel.

The AI can work through up to 50 tool rounds per message, then offers a Continue button (configurable in Settings → AI). Security fixes: AI file tools never follow symlinks or bypass the CI/hooks protection with absolute paths; secrets no longer reach the AI provider through the search index, git history or unredacted tool output; MCP tools ask before running unless you trust the server; and the approval card shows the exact SQL, manifest or command. The AppImage now starts, Fedora upgrades no longer remove the app, and the app finishes starting up without a keyring service.
The explorer stays pinned to the top of the sidebar when every folder section is collapsed.
Collapsing a folder section in the explorer now shrinks it to its header so the other folders get the space.

The file explorer can show more than one folder: File → Add Folder to Explorer… stacks extra folders beneath the project, each with its own collapsible tree. Right-click a folder header to make it the project or remove it; extra folders are remembered across restarts.

The file explorer now shows dotfiles such as .env, .gitignore and .github (caches and .git stay hidden), with an eye button in the header to hide them again. Windows portability fixes from the new cross-platform CI job.

Inline diagnostics in the editor (ruff squiggles, hover messages, Fix with AI, auto-fixes, F8), a trimmed activity bar with a Settings → Panels page, per-project chat history, SSH sessions from the terminal and the AWS panel (SSH / Session Manager), a startup timer plus fixes that show the window about three times sooner, and macOS/Windows portability groundwork.
The video editor moves off the activity bar to View → Video Editor… and the command palette, leaving the bar to code tools.
Fixes the terminal opening with no height (button lit, nothing shown) after a session was saved with it hidden.
"Send selection to AI" and "Restart terminal" now work from the popped-out terminal window.
Fixes the terminal appearing blank in 0.18.6, keeps its content when the pane is resized or shown, and makes sure it stays hidden on every launch until you open it.
The terminal pane gets a header with pop-out (move the live shell into its own window and back), expand to fill the column, and close.
The terminal now stays out of the way until you need it: hidden by default, opened from a new button at the bottom of the activity bar (or Ctrl+`), and remembered across sessions.

Focus mode: expand the editor to the whole window from the tab bar or Ctrl+Shift+X. Tool approvals are now proper cards showing the exact command or file, with a warning for destructive commands, and the activity log says what actually ran.

GNOME-style window title bars on Wayland that follow the desktop's dark/light preference; the default model prefers the API-key provider over the throttled subscription login; the Settings dialog shows the real version; and error messages point at the correct Settings section and console URL.

Fixes Claude models failing on every message with the newer Anthropic SDK. The window title bar and native menus now follow the app theme, the stray line above the editor tabs is gone, and the status bar matches the rest of the dark palette.
Crisper explorer toolbar icons (New File, New Folder, Refresh, Collapse All) and a cleaner Explorer icon in the activity bar.

A large reliability release. The Docker, Kubernetes and CI/CD panels no longer freeze the window and their background refreshes actually update the UI; failed saves, unreadable files and other errors are reported instead of silently ignored; closing the window prompts about unsaved changes; the editor, terminal and AI options in Settings now take effect; the light theme renders correctly throughout; project search runs in the background; user messages can be edited and resent; and subscription sign-in works without a restart. Under the hood, terminal shells and AI-run commands are cleaned up properly and a corrupt setting can no longer block startup.

Arduino panel fixes: board detection no longer reports legacy motherboard serial ports as a connected board, an unrecognised USB device now clearly asks you to pick your board instead of showing a false success, two-line hints are no longer clipped, and the starter tiles lead with the classic Arduino blink. The app is also installable from PyPI with pipx.

Cleaner professional interface with the last emoji replaced by proper icons and status marks, a new documentation site, install via the hosted APT/RPM package repositories with automatic updates, and fixes to status-color rendering in the Docker and Kubernetes panels.

AI answers become project-aware (auto-attached relevant files), image attachments now work with Claude and Gemini, per-hunk apply for AI-proposed changes, Tab accepts inline completions, and a rich diff preview on tool approvals.

Editor find and replace, git pull/fetch and per-file diffs, full-text conversation search, Markdown export, live model list, clickable review findings, and new editor/notification settings. Plus fixes: save events now refresh the Git and Test panels, honest keyring warnings, and corrected usage pricing.
In-app release update notifier, theme-token overhaul, vector icons across the UI, and packaging fixes for offline installs.
First release as Polyglot AI (renamed from Codex Desktop).
